items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: And Arif, Tom Dowd and I, me being the low man on that totem pole, were the non-owners who produced for the label.

ctx.x: You mean they started telling you how to — © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Pretty much, and also we didn’t get along personally. So it was weird. Had I been a better politician I might have navigated those waters better, but I wouldn’t change the records I was making. You know, and I work a certain way. It’s not that it’s good or bad or better or worse or anything, it’s the only way I know how. And you know I would mix a record and someone would say make this louder, make this softer. I’d do a song and someone would say don’t — I wasn’t hired on that basis and plus, Atlantic had gone…
Were you there when they signed Aretha?
